s: For what is Narasapur in Andhra Pradesh known?
x: Narasapur is known for crochet lace; Eluru for carpets, Udayagiri for wooden cutlery and Etikoppaka for lacquerware toys.

s: GI-tagged Etikoppaka lacquerware toys belong to which district?
x: Etikoppaka is in Anakapalli district, not Guntur.

s: For what is the Machilipatnam-Pedana Kalamkari tradition known?
x: Machilipatnam-Pedana Kalamkari is block-printed, while Srikalahasti is known for pen or freehand Kalamkari.

s: Kondapalli toys are made from which light wood?
x: Kondapalli toys use the light Tella Poniki wood.

s: Budithi, known for GI-tagged bell and brass craft, lies in which district?
x: Budithi bell and brass craft is from Srikakulam district (GI 2008).

s: With which place is pen (freehand) Kalamkari associated?
x: Srikalahasti Kalamkari is pen-drawn; Machilipatnam-Pedana is block-printed.

s: For what is Udayagiri in Andhra Pradesh known?
x: Udayagiri is known for wooden cutlery (APPSC 2025); Narasapur is crochet.

s: Where did the Eluru carpet designs 'Farishkhani' and 'Ashunkhani' attract attention?
x: Farishkhani and Ashunkhani, designs of Eluru carpets, attracted attention at the London Exhibition of 1851.

s: Which artisan castes made up the 'Panchanam varu' of Andhra?
o: Potter, weaver, washerman, barber and carpenter
Blacksmith, goldsmith, brazier, carpenter and sculptor
Weaver, dyer, potter, oil-presser and toddy tapper
Goldsmith, potter, weaver, barber and mason
x: Panchanam varu were the five artisan castes: blacksmith, goldsmith, brazier, carpenter and sculptor.

s: Which of the following items from Andhra Pradesh does NOT have a GI tag?
x: Tirupati Laddu (2009), Bandar Laddu (2017) and Banganapalle mango (2017) have GI tags; Tapeswaram Kaja has none.

s: In which year did Bandar Laddu receive its GI tag?
x: Bandar Laddu and Banganapalle mango were GI-tagged in 2017; Tirupati Laddu in 2009.

s: In which district is Kondapalli, known for its GI-tagged toys, located?
x: Kondapalli, whose toys are made of light Tella Poniki wood, is in NTR district.

s: In which year did Budithi bell and brass craft receive its GI tag?
x: Budithi bell and brass craft of Srikakulam got its GI tag in 2008.

s: In which year did Tirupati Laddu receive its GI tag?
x: Tirupati Laddu got its GI tag in 2009; Bandar Laddu and Banganapalle mango in 2017.

s: Which is the state nodal agency for handicrafts in Andhra Pradesh, selling under the name 'Lepakshi'?
x: Lepakshi, run by the A.P. Handicrafts Development Corporation (APHDC), is the state handicrafts nodal agency.

s: Where was a 90-foot installation of Etikoppaka toys unveiled in August 2026?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
x: On 2 August 2026 a 90-foot Etikoppaka toy installation was unveiled at Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram.

s: Which of the following is an Andhra Pradesh craft tradition rather than a Telangana one?
x: Dharmavaram sarees are an Andhra Pradesh tradition; Bidri, Cherial scrolls and Nirmal paintings are associated with Telangana.

s: Which of the following crafts belongs to Telangana and not Andhra Pradesh?
x: Nirmal paintings, Bidri and Cherial scrolls are Telangana crafts.

s: For what is Uppada on the Andhra coast known?
x: Uppada is known for Jamdani silk sarees; Kalamkari is Machilipatnam's and salt Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam's.

s: Which of the following pairs (centre - product) is correctly matched?
x: Machilipatnam is known for Kalamkari; Uppada for Jamdani and Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam for salt.

s: Which state cultural festival is held on the Beach Road and run by APTDC and VMRDA?
x: Visakha Utsav is held on Beach Road, Visakhapatnam, by APTDC and VMRDA.

s: Where is the Rayalaseema Food and Dance Festival held?
x: The Rayalaseema Food and Dance Festival is held at Tirupati in October.

s: 'From Sea to Summit' was the theme of the 2026 edition of which festival?
x: Visakha Utsav 2026 (24 Jan-1 Feb) had the theme 'From Sea to Summit'.

s: The heritage of which region does Lepakshi Utsav (Lepakshi Vaibhavam) showcase?
x: Lepakshi Utsav showcases Rayalaseema heritage, dance and crafts.

s: The Sirimanu utsavam is the chief ritual of which festival?
x: Sirimanu utsavam belongs to Paidithalli Ammavaru of Vizianagaram, not the Gangamma Jatara of Tirupati.

s: Where is Gangamma Jatara, a nine-day fair with men in women's attire, held?
x: Gangamma Jatara is held at Tirupati; Sirimanu belongs to Paidithalli of Vizianagaram.

s: The Mahanandi Shiva temple fair is held in which district?
x: Mahanandi is in Nandyal district.

s: The ancient Kotappakonda tirunallu is held in which district?
x: Kotappakonda is in the Guntur region, now Palnadu district.

s: During the Tirupati Gangamma Jatara, men dress in women's attire. What is this called?
x: In the nine-day Gangamma Jatara men wear women's attire (Perantalu Vesham); Chapparalu are bamboo structures.

s: Which deity is worshipped at Kotappakonda?
x: Kotappakonda in Palnadu is a Shiva (Trikoteswara) centre famous for Maha Sivaratri prabhas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Dwaraka Tirumala is known as Dakshina Dwaraka. Draksharamam is Dakshina Kasi and Srikalahasti is Dakshina Kailasam.

s: Which temple town is called 'Dakshina Kasi'?
x: Draksharamam is Dakshina Kasi; Srikalahasti is Dakshina Kailasam.

s: Which temple town has the epithet 'Dakshina Kailasam'?
x: Srikalahasti is called Dakshina Kailasam.

s:
Consider the following statements about temple-town epithets:
1. Dwaraka Tirumala is called Dakshina Dwaraka.
2. Draksharamam is called Dakshina Kailasam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Dwaraka Tirumala is Dakshina Dwaraka; Draksharamam is Dakshina Kasi, while Srikalahasti is Dakshina Kailasam.

s: In which district is Dwaraka Tirumala, called 'Dakshina Dwaraka', located?
x: Dwaraka Tirumala, the Dakshina Dwaraka, is in Eluru district.

s: Who among the following staged the Tamil folk dance-drama Kuravanji at Kalakshetra?
x: Rukmini Devi Arundale of Kalakshetra staged the Kuravanji, the Tamil form of the Telugu Koravanji.

s: Kuravanji, the Tamil folk dance-drama, corresponds to which Telugu form?
x: The Telugu Koravanji has its Tamil counterpart in the Kuravanji dance-drama.

s: The village of Kuchipudi is associated with which district?
x: Kuchipudi village is associated with Krishna district; the dance is one of India's eight classical forms.

s: Unlike Bharatanatyam's solo temple-dance tradition, what kind of tradition is Kuchipudi of Andhra?
x: Kuchipudi is an Andhra dance-drama tradition, while Bharatanatyam is associated with Tamil Nadu and solo temple dance.

s: What does 'Tarangam' refer to in a Kuchipudi performance?
o: A sequence performed only with geometric movements
Dancing on the rim of a brass plate
x: Tarangam is a distinctive Kuchipudi feature in which the dancer performs while dancing on the rim of a brass plate.

s: Lakumadevi, famed for Bharatanatyam, was a court dancer of which ruler?
x: Lakumadevi was the court dancer of the Reddi king Kumaragiri Reddy. Krishnadevaraya was the Vijayanagara emperor, Tana Shah gifted the Kuchipudi village to performers, and Prolaya Vema Reddi founded the Reddi kingdom.

s: By what old name was the village of Kuchipudi known?
x: Kuchipudi, the village in Krishna district that gave the dance its name, was called Kuchelapuram.

s: By what name is the Makar Sankranti harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu?
x: Sankranti is celebrated as Pongal in Tamil Nadu, as Magh Bihu in Assam and as Uttarayan in Gujarat.

s: Which Reddi king styled himself 'Karpura Vasantarayalu'?
x: Kumaragiri Reddy used this title; merchant Avachi Tippayashetti headed the Sugandhabhandagara that supplied the Vasantotsavam.

s: In which month does Atla Taddi, a women's festival of Andhra, fall?
x: Atla Taddi is a women's festival of Ashwayuja, not Chaitra.

s: Who headed the Sugandhabhandagara that supplied the Vasantotsavam?
x: Merchant Avachi Tippayashetti headed the Sugandhabhandagara (perfume store).

s: Kolla Pandalu (cockfights) are part of which festival?
x: Kolla Pandalu and Pottella Pandalu are part of the January Sankranti festival.

s: Of which state are Bathukamma and Bonalu identity festivals?
x: Bathukamma and Bonalu are Telangana identity festivals.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra festivals?
o: Vasantotsavam was most popular under the Reddi kings
Atla Taddi falls in the month of Chaitra
Kumaragiri Reddy styled himself Karpura Vasantarayalu
Sankranti is a January harvest festival
x: Atla Taddi is a women's festival of Ashwayuja, not Chaitra.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a marker of Telangana culture?
x: Bathukamma, Oggu Katha and Cherial are listed as Telangana markers. Kolatam kirtanas are associated with group dance in the Andhra folk-song context.

s: Which statement about the Gathasaptasati is correct?
o: It records couple and choir dances of rural folk.
It describes only lullabies sung by women.
It records only court dances of professional artists.
It is Biruduraju Ramaraju's book on folk theory.
x: The Gathasaptasati records couple and choir dances of rural folk.

s: Who wrote the first book on the theory of folk knowledge in Telugu?
x: It was written by Biruduraju Ramaraju; Annamacharya wrote Kolatam kirtanas.

s: On which date is World Folk Day observed?
x: World Folk Day falls on 22 August.

s: What are 'Jola patalu' in Andhra folk culture?
x: Jola patalu are lullabies.

s: Who wrote the Kolatam kirtanas, sung for the group stick dance?
x: Annamacharya wrote the Kolatam kirtanas.

s: With which occasion are Sankranti songs and Gangireddulaata associated?
x: Sankranti songs and Gangireddulaata belong to the January harvest festival.

s: Kolattam (Dandalasyam) was the main dance of which era?
x: Kolattam was the main dance of the Eastern Chalukya era, not the Kakatiya era.

s: Which Andhra folk performance features a decorated bull and is associated with Sankranti?
x: Gangireddulu features a decorated bull at Sankranti; Butta Bommalu uses large figures, Dappu is percussion-led and Garagalu involves pots for the village goddess.

s: Dhimsa, performed by tribal women of the Araku or Alluri Sitarama Raju district, is traced to which place?
x: The origin of Dhimsa is traced to Koraput in Odisha, although it is strongly associated with the tribal women of the Araku and ASR region.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Puli Veshalu — Namala village solo dance
x: Tappeta Gullu is associated with the north coastal districts. Dhimsa is associated with tribal women of Araku, Keelugurram is popular in Guntur and Puli Veshalu is the Vizianagaram tiger dance.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Lambadi is the dance of the Banjara community. Dommarata is acrobatics, Chekka Bhajana uses wooden clappers and Keelugurram is the Guntur dummy-horse dance.

s: Kolattam of Andhra is similar to which dance of Karnataka?
x: Kolattam corresponds to Jadakollu in Karnataka.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Puli Veshalu is the tiger dance of Vizianagaram Dasara; Keelugurram is of Guntur and Namala Singadu of Anantapur.

s: In whose honour do Garagalu dancers carry decorated pots on the head?
x: Garagalu dancers carry decorated pots on the head for the village goddess.

s: To which region does Tappeta Gullu, in which shepherds invoke rain and appease Gangamma, belong?
x: Tappeta Gullu is a dance of the north coastal districts.

s: What is the leader of a Kolattam group called?
x: The Kolattam (Dandalasyam) group of 8 or 12 dancers is led by the Pennadi.

s: How many dancers usually make up a Kolattam group?
x: Kolattam is a stick dance of 8 or 12 dancers.

s: Keelugurram (Ashwa Nrutyam), the dummy-horse dance, is associated with which district?
x: Keelugurram, the dummy-horse dance, belongs to Guntur.

s: Namala Singadu Nrutyam, a solo dance from Namala village, belongs to which district?
x: Namala Singadu Nrutyam is a solo dance from Namala village, Anantapur.

s: In which folk dance of Andhra do dancers wear large hollow figures or masks?
x: In Butta Bommalu dancers wear large hollow figures/masks; Garagalu uses pots on the head.

s: Which dynasty ruled Berar, the Deccan Sultanate that stayed out of the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
x: Berar was ruled by the Imad Shahis and stayed out; Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance.

s: From which Sultanate was Jagadeva Rao, whose shelter by Rama Raya helped provoke the Deccan coalition, a rebel?
x: Rama Raya sheltered Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda, one of the causes of the coalition.

s: Which region did Rama Raya acquire in 1546-47 by backing Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar?
x: In 1546-47 Rama Raya supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the Raichur doab.

s: Who was the key organiser of the Deccan Sultanates' alliance that fought at Talikota (1565)?
x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda was the key organiser of the coalition.

s: Which statement about the aftermath of Talikota is correct?
o: Sewell held that the capital suffered no destruction.
The sack is universally held to have wiped out Vijayanagara culture.
Tirumala wrote the account of the sack in 1570.
Sewell called the sacked city a 'graveyard', a view that may be exaggerated.
x: Sewell used the expression 'graveyard' for the sacked capital, though that assessment may be exaggerated.

s: Which of the following pairs (Sultanate – Ruler at Talikota) is correctly matched?
x: Bijapur was ruled by Ali Adil Shah. Ahmadnagar was under Hussain Nizam Shah, Golconda under Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Bidar under Ali Barid Shah.

s: Who among the following was married to Chand Bibi among the marriage alliances before Talikota?
x: Chand Bibi married Ali Adil Shah, while Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

s: For how long was Hampi looted after the Battle of Talikota?
x: Hampi was looted for about six months; the damage was severe but not total.

s: Which historian named the Battle of 1565 'Rakshasi-Tangadi'?
x: Heras called it Rakshasi-Tangadi; Sewell used Talikota and Sherwani used Bannihatti.

s: Who beheaded Aliya Rama Raya at the Battle of Talikota?
x: Hussain Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar beheaded Rama Raya; Ibrahim Qutb Shah was the alliance's main organiser.

s:
Consider the following statements about Aliya Rama Raya:
1. He ruled as regent of Sadasiva Raya.
2. Between 1557 and 1563 he backed Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar.
3. He gave shelter to Jagadeva Rao, a rebel of Golconda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Rama Raya was Sadasiva's regent, razed Ahmadnagar with Bijapur in 1557-63 and sheltered Jagadeva Rao.

s: Who called the Vijayanagara capital after Talikota a 'graveyard'?
x: Robert Sewell called the city a 'graveyard', a view that may be exaggerated.

s: In which year was the Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) fought?
x: The Battle of Talikota was fought on 23 January 1565 between Vijayanagara and the Deccan Sultanates.

s: Aliya Rama Raya, the regent at the time of Talikota, was the son-in-law of which ruler?
x: Aliya ('son-in-law') Rama Raya was the son-in-law of Krishnadevaraya.

s: Where did Sadasiva and Tirumala flee after the defeat at Talikota?
x: They fled to Penukonda; Chandragiri became a capital later, under Venkata II.

s: In order of succession, which ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara was the Aravidu dynasty?
x: The Aravidu dynasty was the fourth dynasty of Vijayanagara and ruled from 1570 to 1680 with seven rulers.

s: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570?
x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Toppur:
1. It was fought in 1616 and is called the 'second Talikota'.
2. Mir Jumla was killed in this battle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Jagga Raya was killed at Toppur; Mir Jumla later defeated Sriranga III at Vandavasi (1642). So 1 only (A).

s:
Consider the following statements about Sriranga Raya III:
1. He was the last ruler of the Aravidu dynasty.
2. He was defeated at Vandavasi (1642) by Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: he was defeated at Vandavasi by Mir Jumla of Golconda. So 1 only (A).

s: Which Vijayanagara ruler was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja'?
x: Venkatapati Raya II was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja' (and 'Second Krishnadevaraya').

s: Which pair of leaders won the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
o: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore
Mir Jumla and Sriranga Raya III
Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka and Veerappa Nayaka
x: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore won the Battle of Toppur in 1616.

s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara derived its name from which place?
x: The dynasty was named after Araviti, also called Aravidu, a village in Kurnool district.

s: Which Aravidu ruler lost Kondaveedu to Ibrahim Qutb Shah?
x: Sriranga I (1572-85), eldest son of Tirumala, lost Kondaveedu to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

s: Who killed Sriranga II, who ruled briefly in 1614?
x: Sriranga II was killed by Jagga Raya, who was himself killed at Toppur in 1616.

s: To which place did the Aravidu rulers move their capital in 1600?
x: The capitals shifted Hampi, Penukonda (1570), Chandragiri (Venkata II) and Vellore (1600).

s:
Arrange the capitals of Vijayanagara after Hampi in chronological order:
1. Vellore
2. Penukonda
3. Chandragiri
x: The order was Penukonda (1570) under Tirumala, then Chandragiri under Venkata II, then Vellore (1600).

s:
Arrange the following Aravidu rulers in chronological order:
1. Sriranga III
2. Tirumala Raya
3. Venkatapati Raya II
4. Sriranga I
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Tirumala Raya (1570) founded the dynasty, followed by Sriranga I, then Venkatapati Raya II (1585-1614); Sriranga III was the last.

s: Under which Aravidu ruler did Chandragiri become the capital of Vijayanagara?
x: The capital moved from Penukonda to Chandragiri under Venkatapati Raya II, and later to Vellore.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vilapakam inscription?
o: It gives the genealogy of the Tuluva dynasty
It is mainly a genealogy of the Qutb Shahi dynasty
It gives the genealogy of the Aravidu dynasty
x: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 gives the genealogy of the Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties, not of the Qutb Shahis.

s: Where did Venkatapati Raya II permit the Dutch to trade?
x: Venkatapati Raya II permitted Dutch trade at Pulicat and also allowed Jesuit churches at Nellore and Chandragiri.

s: To the reign of which ruler does the Siddhavatam fort inscription of 1605 belong?
x: Both the Vilapakam (1601) and Siddhavatam (1605) inscriptions belong to Venkatapati Raya II.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Venkatapati Raya II?
o: He allowed the Dutch to trade at Pulicat
He allowed Jesuit churches at Nellore and Chandragiri
He granted Madras to Francis Day
x: Madras was granted in 1639 by Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka in Venkatapati Raya III's reign, not by Venkatapati II.

s: Which title, besides 'Second Andhra Bhoja', was given to Venkatapati Raya II?
x: Venkatapati Raya II was called the 'Second Krishnadevaraya' and 'Second Andhra Bhoja'.

s: To the reign of which Vijayanagara ruler does the Vilapakam inscription of 1601 belong?
x: The Vilapakam inscription (1601), giving the Tuluva and Aravidu genealogy, belongs to Venkatapati Raya II.

s: At whose court did Appayya Dikshita, author of Shaivarka Mani Dipika, live?
x: Appayya Dikshita was a scholar at the court of Venkatapati Raya II.

s: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka granted Madras to Francis Day in 1639 during the reign of which Vijayanagara ruler?
x: The 1639 grant of Madras to Francis Day of the Machilipatnam council came in the reign of Venkatapati Raya III.

s: To whom was the site of Madras granted in 1639?
x: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka granted Madras to Francis Day of the English East India Company in 1639.

s:
Consider the following statements about the grant of Madras (1639):
1. It was granted by Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka.
2. The grantee belonged to the English Company's Machilipatnam council.
3. Venkatapati Raya II issued it personally.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The grant was by the local Nayaka Damarla Venkatadri to Francis Day of the Machilipatnam council, in Venkatapati III's reign, not by the king himself.

s: From which place did the Damarla Nayaks, who granted the site of Madras, rule?
x: The Damarla Nayaks, Velama feudatories of the Aravidus, ruled from Srikalahasti.

s: Who founded the Nayaka kingdom of Tanjore?
x: Tanjore was founded by Sevappa Nayaka; Madurai by Vishwanatha Nayaka, Gingee by Krishnappa Nayaka and Mysore by Raja Wodeyar.

s: Who was the rebel father whose capture earned Vishwanatha Nayaka the grant of Madurai?
x: Vishwanatha Nayaka captured his rebel father Nagama and was granted Madurai; his son Krishnappa Nayaka made it independent c. 1565.

s: Who built the Tirumala Rayala Mahal at Madurai?
x: Tirumala Nayaka, who ruled Madurai from 1623 to 1659, built the Tirumala Rayala Mahal.

s: After Vijayanagara weakened, which hereditary class did the amara-nayakas become, the forerunners of the zamindars?
x: The amara-nayakas developed into hereditary Palegars, who were the forerunners of the zamindars.

s: At Gandikota in 1657, who is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon?
x: Mir Jumla of Golconda is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon at Gandikota in 1657.

s: Who founded the Nayaka kingdom of Gingee?
x: Krishnappa Nayaka founded Gingee; Sevappa founded Tanjore and Vishwanatha founded Madurai.

s: During whose reign did Sevappa Nayaka found the Tanjore Nayaka kingdom?
x: Tanjore under Sevappa Nayaka is placed in Achyutaraya's time; Mysore was founded under Venkata II.

s: Who made the Madurai Nayaka kingdom independent around 1565?
x: Vishwanatha's son Krishnappa made Madurai independent c. 1565.

s: Which of the following pairs (Nayaka kingdom – Founder) is correctly matched?
x: Ikkeri (Keladi) was founded by Chowdappa Nayaka; Tanjore by Sevappa, Gingee by Krishnappa and Madurai by Vishwanatha.

s: From which of the following did the hereditary Palegars, forerunners of zamindars like those of Kalahasti and Chittoor, grow?
x: Amara-nayakas became hereditary Palegars, the forerunners of zamindaris such as Kalahasti and Chittoor.

s: Govinda Dikshita, author of Sahitya Sudha, was the minister of which Nayaka rulers?
x: Govinda Dikshita was minister of the Tanjore Nayaks and wrote Sahitya Sudha on Achyutappa and Raghunatha Nayaka.

s: Who among the following wrote Sahitya Sudha on Achyutappa and Raghunatha Nayaka of Tanjore?
x: Sahitya Sudha was written by Govinda Dikshita, minister of the Tanjore Nayaks.

s: Kshetrayya, the Telugu padam composer linked with Movva in Krishna district, used which name of the deity as his signature (mudra)?
x: Kshetrayya signed his padams with Muvva Gopala, Krishna of Muvva (Movva).

s: Who was the last Nayaka king of Tanjore, at whose court Kshetrayya composed padams?
x: Vijayaraghava Nayaka, the last Nayaka king of Tanjore, was a patron of Kshetrayya.

s: Who is the author of Shaivarka Mani Dipika?
x: Shaivarka Mani Dipika is the work of Appayya Dikshita; Vasucharitra is associated with Ramaraja Bhushanudu.

s: Who is the author of the Telugu work Vasucharitra?
x: Vasucharitra is by Ramaraja Bhushanudu; Appayya Dikshita wrote Shaivarka Mani Dipika.

s: Through the courts of which rulers did Raya gopurams and kalyana mandapas mainly spread after Vijayanagara?
x: Vijayanagara temple forms such as Raya gopurams and kalyana mandapas spread via the Nayaka courts.

s: Which European visitor left an eyewitness account of the ruined Vijayanagara capital in 1567?
x: Caesar Frederick, a Venetian merchant, visited Vijayanagara in 1567 and left an eyewitness account of the ruined capital.

s: Who surveyed and mapped the ruins of Hampi in 1800?
x: Colin Mackenzie surveyed and mapped the Hampi ruins in 1800 and later became the first Surveyor General of India.

s: Colin Mackenzie, who mapped Hampi in 1800, later became the first holder of which post in India?
x: Colin Mackenzie surveyed Hampi in 1800 and later became the first Surveyor General of India.

s: Who is the author of 'A Forgotten Empire' (1900) on Vijayanagara?
x: Robert Sewell wrote A Forgotten Empire in 1900.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Caesar Frederick — Founder of the Aravidu dynasty
x: Caesar Frederick was a Venetian merchant who recorded an eyewitness account in 1567; Tirumala, not Caesar Frederick, founded the Aravidu line.

s: In which year was the Battle of Khanwa fought?
x: First Panipat was 1526, Khanwa 1527, Chanderi 1528 and Ghaghra 1529.

s: In which battle did Babur defeat Medini Rai in 1528?
x: Medini Rai was defeated at Chanderi (1528); Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527) and the Afghans at Ghaghra (1529).

s: After which battle did Babur take the title 'Ghazi'?
x: Babur declared Jehad and took the title Ghazi at Khanwa (1527), not Panipat.

s: Whom did Babur defeat in the Battle of Ghaghra (1529)?
x: At Ghaghra in 1529 Babur defeated the Afghans.

s: Why is the Battle of Khanwa regarded as more decisive than the First Battle of Panipat?
o: Artillery was used in India for the first time in it
Ibrahim Lodi was killed in it
Rana Sanga was a stronger enemy and its result set up Mughal supremacy in North India
x: At Khanwa (1527) Babur broke Rajput power under Rana Sanga, a stronger foe than Ibrahim Lodi, and set Mughal rule on firm ground.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat.
2. Babur defeated Rana Sanga in the Battle of Khanwa.
3. Babur assumed the title of Ghazi after the Battle of Khanwa.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at First Panipat, then Rana Sanga at Khanwa, after which he took the title Ghazi.

s: Besides Daulat Khan Lodi and Alam Khan, who invited Babur to India?
x: The three inviters were Daulat Khan Lodi (Governor of Punjab), Alam Khan (Ibrahim Lodi's uncle) and Rana Sanga of Mewar.

s: Which nickname did Babur earn by his lavish distribution of the Lodi treasure after Panipat?
x: Lavish sharing of the treasure earned him the nickname 'Qalandar'; 'Ghazi' was the title taken after Khanwa.

s: Whom did Babur defeat at the Battle of Chanderi (1528)?
x: Babur defeated Medini Rai at Chanderi in 1528.

s: Who led Akbar's army at Haldighati (1576)?
x: Man Singh led Akbar's army against Maharana Pratap at Haldighati in 1576.

s: Who backed Mahmud Lodi's Afghans at the Battle of Ghaghra (1529)?
x: At Ghaghra Babur defeated Mahmud Lodi's Afghans backed by Nusrat Shah of Bengal.

s: Which of the following pairs (Battle – Opponent of the Mughals) is correctly matched?
x: Humayun lost Chausa (1539) to Sher Shah; Khanwa was against Rana Sanga, Chanderi against Medini Rai and Panipat II against Hemu.

s:
Arrange the following battles of Babur in chronological order:
1. Khanwa
2. Ghaghra
3. First Battle of Panipat
4. Chanderi
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Panipat I (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528) and Ghaghra (1529).

s: Which Mughal ruler was defeated by Sher Shah in the Battle of Kannauj (Bilgram) in 1540?
x: At Kannauj (Bilgram) in 1540 Sher Shah defeated Humayun, who then went into exile.

s: At Panipat I, Babur's army of about 12,000 faced about how many of Ibrahim Lodi's troops?
x: Babur's 12,000 men faced about 1,00,000 troops of Ibrahim Lodi.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the First Battle of Panipat?
o: It saw the first large-scale use of field artillery in North India
x: Babur's side used no war elephants at Panipat; the Rumi carts sheltered guns, not elephants.

s: Which two cities did Babur gain after the First Battle of Panipat?
x: After defeating Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526, Babur took Delhi and Agra along with the Lodi treasure.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Tulughma – Flanking units wheeling round to encircle the enemy
Rumi method (araba) – War elephants chained together as a barrier
Ustad Ali and Mustafa – Ottoman gunners commanding Babur's artillery
x: The Rumi method (araba) chained carts, not elephants, as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns.

s: Which statement regarding Babur’s use of artillery at Panipat is correct?
o: It was commanded by Ibrahim Lodi’s Ottoman officers.
It was used exclusively against cavalry and not infantry.
It marked the first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare.
It was the first use of any firearm ever known in India.
x: Panipat marked the first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare. Firearms were not wholly unknown in India before Babur.

s: Of which origin was the tulughma tactic used by Babur?
x: Tulughma (flanks wheeling to encircle) was Uzbek; the Rumi/araba carts were Ottoman.

s: Who commanded Babur's artillery at Panipat?
x: Ottoman gunners Ustad Ali and Mustafa commanded Babur's artillery.

s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's warfare:
1. Gunpowder and firearms were not wholly unknown in India before Babur.
2. Babur's Rumi carts were a barrier against war elephants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gunpowder was known before Babur (used against fort walls); the Rumi carts were a barrier for guns and matchlockmen, not against elephants.

s: Who joined the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga at the Battle of Khanwa?
o: Daulat Khan Lodi and Medini Rai
Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati
x: Rana Sanga’s coalition included the Afghan Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati.

s: Which title did Babur take after his victory at Khanwa?
x: After Khanwa Babur took the title 'Ghazi'; before the battle he had declared jihad, renounced wine and remitted tamgha for Muslims.

s: At Khanwa, against which of Rana Sanga's forces did Babur mainly use trenches and barricades?
x: Babur used trenches and barricades against Rana Sanga's elephants; his artillery also played a decisive role.

s: Before Khanwa, Babur remitted which tax for Muslims as part of his religious appeal?
x: Babur declared jihad, renounced wine and remitted the tamgha (trade tax) for Muslims before Khanwa.

s:
Consider the following statements about the establishment of the Mughal Empire:
1. Khanwa, more than Panipat, firmly established Mughal power in India.
2. Babur set up a well-organised administrative system before his death.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Khanwa (1527) broke Rajput power and firmly established the Mughals, but Babur's four-year rule left no administrative system.

s: Which was the first major field-artillery battle in North India?
x: Panipat I, in which Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Delhi Sultan, was the first major field-artillery battle in North India.

s: Of which origin was the Rumi method of warfare used by Babur?
x: The Rumi method (carts linked as a barrier for matchlockmen and artillery) was Ottoman; Tulughma was Uzbek.

s: Which inviter of Babur was the Governor of Punjab?
x: Daulat Khan Lodi, Governor of Punjab, invited Babur along with Alam Khan and Rana Sanga.

s: What was Alam Khan, one of those who invited Babur, to Ibrahim Lodi?
x: Alam Khan was Ibrahim Lodi's uncle; Daulat Khan Lodi was the Governor of Punjab.

s: Of which origin was Babur's tulughma tactic, in which flanks wheel round to encircle the enemy?
x: Tulughma was Uzbek; the Rumi (araba) method was Ottoman.

s: Which cities did Babur occupy after the First Battle of Panipat?
x: After Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra.

s: After which battle did Babur take the title 'Ghazi'?
x: Babur took the title Ghazi after Khanwa (1527) and the title Padshah at Kabul in 1507.

s: From whom did Babur trace his descent?
o: Chingiz Khan on his father's side and Timur on his mother's side
Timur on his father's side and Chingiz Khan on his mother's side
x: Babur was descended from Timur through his father and from Chingiz Khan through his mother.

s: Where was Babur born in 1483?
x: Babur was born in Farghana in Central Asia in 1483.

s: The Mughals were Chagatai Turks. After whom was the Chagatai line named?
o: The second son of Chingiz Khan
The founder of the Uzbek khanate
x: Chagatai was Genghis (Chingiz) Khan's second son, ruler of Central Asia and Turkistan.

s: What does the name 'Babur' mean?
x: Babur, the nickname of Zahir-ud-din Muhammad, means tiger.

s: Which of the following statements about Babur’s relations with the Deccan is correct?
o: Babur made Golconda his provincial capital.
Babur defeated Sultan Quli of Golconda at Ghaghra.
The Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan during Babur’s time.
Babur conquered the Deccan before the Battle of Khanwa.
x: The Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan during Babur’s time. Babur was a contemporary of Krishnadevaraya and Golconda’s Sultan Quli.

s: In his account of India, Babur praised which ruler as the most powerful?
x: Babur praised Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara as the most powerful ruler in India.

s: In which year did Babur take the title 'Padshah' at Kabul?
x: Babur became Padshah at Kabul in 1507 and took the title Ghazi after Khanwa in 1527.

s: Babur died at Agra in 1530. Where was he buried?
x: Babur died at Agra but lies buried at Kabul (Bagh-e-Babur).

s: Under which ruler was the Mansabdari system introduced?
x: The Mansabdari system was introduced under Akbar, not during Babur's four-year rule.

s: At Babur's death, his dominions extended from Kabul and Badakhshan to the borders of which region?
x: Babur's dominions ran from Kabul and Badakhshan through Punjab, Delhi and Agra to the borders of Bihar.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a limitation of Babur’s rule in India?
o: The Afghans continued to claim Delhi
Gujarat and Malwa were united under Bahadur Shah
A fully developed administrative system was established
x: D is the answer because Babur set up no administrative system at all (his rule had shallow roots and the treasury was empty), so 'a fully developed administrative system' was not one of his limitations. A, B and C are listed limits: the Afghans still claimed Delhi, Bengal stayed unconquered, and Gujarat-Malwa was united under Bahadur Shah.

s: To whom did Babur give the province of Badakhshan?
x: Babur ruled through jagirs and paraganas, and Badakhshan was given to Humayun.

s: Which is generally identified as the first Mughal garden?
x: Ram Bagh, also called Aram Bagh, at Agra was the first Mughal garden, laid out on the charbagh (four-quartered) plan.

s: Babur introduced which garden plan in India?
x: Babur introduced the charbagh (four-part) garden, as at Ram Bagh, Agra.

s: Where is Babur's Kabuli Bagh mosque, which commemorates the 1526 victory?
x: The Kabuli Bagh mosque at Panipat commemorates the 1526 victory.

s: What were the silver coins that Babur issued in the Timurid style called?
x: Babur issued silver Shahrukhi coins in the Timurid style and introduced the charbagh garden.

s: Where did Babur build the Kabuli Bagh Mosque to commemorate his 1526 victory?
x: The Kabuli Bagh Mosque is at Panipat and marks the 1526 victory; Ram Bagh was at Agra.

s: Who translated the Baburnama into Persian (1589) under Akbar?
x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan translated it into Persian in 1589.

s:
Consider the following statements about English translations of the Baburnama:
1. Leyden and Erskine made the first English translation.
2. Annette Beveridge translated it from the Turki original.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Leyden and Erskine first translated it into English; Annette Beveridge later translated it from the Turki original.

s: According to the Baburnama, India had how many Muslim and Hindu powers?
x: Babur counted five Muslim and two Hindu powers, the Hindu ones being Vijayanagara and Mewar.

s:
Assertion (A): Babur wrote his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi, in Chagatai Turki.
Reason (R): Turki was the court language of the Mughals.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Babur wrote in Chagatai Turki, but the Mughal court language was Persian, so R is false.

s: In which language was the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama) written?
x: The Baburnama was written in Chaghatai Turkish; Persian was the Mughal court language.

s: From where did Humayun drive Mahmud Lodi after defeating the Afghans at the Battle of Dourah (1532)?
x: Dourah (Devara), 1532, on the Gomati, drove Mahmud Lodi from Jaunpur.

s: After which battle did Sher Khan assume the title 'Sher Shah'?
x: He took the title Sher Shah after Chausa (1539); after Kannauj (1540) he took the throne.

s: With whose help did Humayun retake Kandahar and Kabul during his exile?
x: The Safavid Shah Tahmasp of Persia helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gujarat, 1535 — Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu
x: When pressed by Humayun in Gujarat in 1535, Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu. Humayun was defeated at Chausa and Kannauj, while he defeated Sikandar Sur at Sirhind.

s: In which fort was the Sher Mandal library, from whose stairs Humayun fell to his death in January 1556?
x: He fell from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in the Purana Qila, Delhi.

s: By what other name is the Battle of Kannauj (1540), in which Sher Shah defeated Humayun, known?
x: Kannauj is also called the Battle of Bilgram.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rao Jaitsi?
o: He was the ruler of Bikaner
He lost Bikaner to Kamran Mirza in 1534
The Kamran Mirza he fought was Babur's son
x: Rao Jaitsi of Bikaner defeated Babur's son Kamran Mirza in 1534; he did not lose Bikaner to him.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Samugarh?
o: It was fought in 1539 between Babur and Mahmud Lodi.
It was fought in 1540 between Humayun and Sher Khan.
It was fought in 1555 between Humayun and Hemu.
It was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh.
x: The Battle of Samugarh was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh. It was not a battle of Humayun's return in 1555.

s: Where did Humayun defeat Sikandar Sur in 1555?
x: Humayun beat Sikandar Sur at Sirhind in 1555 and retook Delhi and Agra.

s: Where was Akbar born in 1542, during Humayun's exile?
x: Akbar, son of Hamida Banu Begum, was born at Amarkot in 1542; he was crowned at Kalanaur.

s: Where was Akbar crowned after Humayun's death?
x: Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur after Humayun's death in 1556.

s: Which place did Bahadur Shah of Gujarat let the Portuguese fortify in 1535, when pressed by Humayun?
x: Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu; Bhatkal was linked with Krishnadeva Raya.

s:
Arrange the following events of Humayun's reign in chronological order:
1. Battle of Kannauj
2. Siege of Chunar Fort
3. Birth of Akbar at Amarkot
4. Portuguese allowed to fortify Diu
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Chunar siege (1532), Diu fortified (1535), Kannauj (1540) and Akbar's birth at Amarkot (1542).

s: Who among the following was the mother of Akbar?
x: Humayun married Hamida Banu Begum, Akbar's mother; Akbar was born at Amarkot in 1542.

s: Which of the following was NOT a brother of Humayun?
x: Kamran, Askari and Hindal were Humayun's rival brothers; Mirza Hakim was Akbar's half-brother.

s: Which was Babur's last battle, fought in 1529 against the Afghans under Mahmud Lodi?
x: Ghaghra (1529) was Babur's last battle; the order was Panipat I, Khanwa, Chanderi, Ghaghra.

s: During which period did Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, contemporary of Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah, rule Golconda?
x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah ruled Golconda from 1518 to 1543.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Panipat II — Akbar and Sher Shah
x: Panipat II was fought in 1556 between Akbar, represented by Bairam Khan, and Hemu. Sher Shah was the opponent of Humayun at Kannauj.

s: Between Aurangzeb and whom was the Battle of Samugarh (1658) fought?
x: Samugarh (1658) was Aurangzeb vs Dara Shikoh, not a Humayun battle.

s:
Arrange the following battles in chronological order:
1. Haldighati
2. Ghaghra
3. Sirhind
4. Chausa
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Ghaghra (1529), Chausa (1539), Sirhind (1555) and Haldighati (1576).

s: By what name is Sher Shah Suri's Sadak-e-Azam, one of Asia's oldest major roads, better known?
x: The Grand Trunk Road, called Sadak-e-Azam under Sher Shah Suri, is one of Asia's oldest major roads.

s: Of which metal was the dam in Sher Shah's currency made?
x: The rupiya was silver, the dam copper and the mohur gold.

s: Of which metal was Sher Shah's rupiya, weighing about 178 grains, made?
x: The rupiya was a silver coin of about 178 grains; the dam was copper and the mohur gold.

s: Which of the following pairs (Sher Shah's coin – Metal) is correctly matched?
x: The mohur was gold, the rupiya silver and the dam copper.

s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's sarais:
1. They served as dak-chowkis for relaying news and mail.
2. Market towns grew around them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: sarais served as dak-chowkis with horses, and market towns grew around them.

s: Besides lodging travellers, what did Sher Shah's sarais serve as for relaying news and mail?
x: The sarais served as dak-chowkis; market towns also grew around them.

s: Which route did Sher Shah's Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road) cover?
x: The Sadak-e-Azam ran from Sonargaon in Bengal to the Indus; Agra-Burhanpur and Lahore-Multan were other Sur roads.

s: Besides the Sadak-e-Azam, which of the following roads was built by Sher Shah?
x: Sher Shah also built the Agra-Burhanpur, Agra-Jodhpur-Chittor and Lahore-Multan roads, with sarais at intervals.

s: Who among the following built or restored the Sadak-e-Azam, later known as the Grand Trunk Road?
x: Sher Shah built or restored the Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road) and set up sarais along it.

s: Who is the author of the Humayun-nama?
x: The Humayun-nama was written by Humayun's sister Gulbadan Begum. Hamida Banu Begum was Humayun's wife and Akbar's mother; Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama; Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.

s: In which year did Sher Shah build the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila?
x: The Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque dates to 1541, after Chausa (1539) and before Sher Shah's death at Kalinjar (1545).

s: For what is Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram notable?
o: a four-domed marble mausoleum in Agra
an octagonal tomb set in a tank
a circular tomb built inside the Purana Qila
x: The tomb at Sasaram is an octagonal monument surrounded by water in a tank.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Purana Qila – Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque built inside it by Sher Shah
Kalinjar Fort – Sher Khan submitted to Humayun after its siege
Chunar Fort – Sher Shah died during its siege in 1545
Bhatkal Fort – Sher Khan submitted to Humayun after its siege
x: Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila. Sher Khan submitted after the siege of Chunar, Sher Shah died besieging Kalinjar, and Krishnadeva Raya let the Portuguese build at Bhatkal.

s: Near which place is Rohtas Fort, begun by Sher Shah in 1541, located?
x: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, Pakistan, was begun by Sher Shah in 1541 under Todar Mal.

s: Who built Humayun's Tomb in Delhi?
x: Bega Begum (Haji Begum) built Humayun's Tomb; Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama.

s: Who was the architect of Humayun's Tomb?
x: Mirak Mirza Ghiyas designed Humayun's Tomb, built 1565-72.

s: Where is Balban's Tomb, with the first true arch in India, located?
x: Balban's Tomb is at Mehrauli, Delhi; Sasaram has Sher Shah's octagonal tomb.

s: Who began the citadel of Purana Qila (Dinpanah) in Delhi, which was later given its present form by Sher Shah?
x: Humayun began the Dinpanah citadel; Sher Shah gave the Purana Qila its present form.

s: Who completed Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram?
x: Sher Shah began his octagonal tomb at Sasaram; his son Islam Shah completed it.

s: Under whose supervision was the Rohtas Fort near Jhelum begun by Sher Shah in 1541?
x: Rohtas Fort was begun in 1541 under Todar Mal, who later served Akbar.

s: Who built the tomb of Sikandar Lodi in Delhi?
x: Sikandar Lodi's tomb in Delhi was built by his son Ibrahim Lodi.

s: In which year was Humayun's Tomb in Delhi declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Humayun's Tomb became a UNESCO site in 1993; Rohtas Fort followed in 1997.

s: In which year was Sher Shah's Rohtas Fort inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum, Pakistan, became a UNESCO site in 1997.

s: From whom did Farid receive the title 'Sher Khan' for slaying a tiger?
x: The title 'Sher Khan' was given by Bahar Khan of Bihar, not Babur.

s: From whom did Sher Shah take the fort of Raisen?
x: Raisen was taken from Puran Mal.

s: At which battle did Sher Shah fight Maldeo Rathore of Marwar?
x: Sher Shah fought Maldeo Rathore at Samel (Giri-Sumel) in 1544, where Jaita and Kumpa fought bravely.

s: Whose generals were Jaita and Kumpa?
x: Jaita and Kumpa were Maldeo's generals at the hard-fought battle of Samel (1544).

s: What was the original name of Sher Shah Suri?
x: Sher Shah was born Farid (Farid Khan); Jalal Khan was his son Islam Shah.

s: Sher Shah's father was an Afghan jagirdar of which place?
x: Farid was the son of an Afghan jagirdar of Sasaram, of the Sur tribe.

s: Which city, where young Farid (Sher Shah) studied, was called 'Siraj-i-Hind'?
x: Farid studied at Jaunpur, known as Siraj-i-Hind.

s: What was the role of the Fotedar in a Sur-era pargana?
x: The Fotedar was the pargana treasurer; Karkuns were the Hindi and Persian writers.

s: In Sher Shah's army, what did 'dagh' mean?
x: Dagh was the branding of horses; chehra/huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.

s: What did Sher Shah's administration do to stop officers from building local interests?
o: Gave officers their posts for life
Appointed officers in their home areas
x: Officers were frequently transferred so that they did not build local interests.

s: In Sur administration, what did the Chief Shiqdar (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) of a sarkar look after?
x: The Chief Shiqdar handled law and order; the Chief Munsif was the sarkar revenue/civil officer.

s: Which statement about policing under the Sur administration is correct?
o: Public morals were regulated only by village accountants.
Local headmen were made responsible for detecting crime.
Crime detection was entrusted exclusively to the central army.
The Sur rulers had no organised espionage system.
x: Local headmen were held responsible for detecting crime. The system also included censors of public morals and an efficient espionage network.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with Sher Shah's revenue administration?
o: Qanungo — command of the royal cavalry
x: The amin (munsif) of the pargana made the revenue assessment. The shiqdar kept law and order, and the qanungo and patwari kept revenue and local records; none of them prepared manuscripts, commanded the cavalry or minted coins.

s: In Sur administration, what did the Chief Munsif (munsif-i-munsifan) of a sarkar deal with?
x: The Chief Munsif handled revenue and civil matters; the Chief Shiqdar looked after law and order.

s: In Sher Shah's army, what did 'chehra' (huliya) mean?
x: Chehra or huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers; dagh was horse branding. Both checked fraud.

s: In a Sur-era pargana, who were the Karkuns?
o: Writers keeping records in Hindi and Persian
x: Karkuns were writers who kept records in Hindi and Persian.

s: Which measure did Sher Shah's land survey use to measure land uniformly?
x: Land was measured with the sikandari gaz and the jarib, and classified into good, middling and bad.

s: In Sher Shah's revenue system, what was the Qabuliyat?
o: the title deed given to the peasant stating his revenue dues
the deed of agreement signed by the peasant accepting the revenue demand
the fee paid to the surveyor
the fee paid to the revenue collector
x: The Qabuliyat was the peasant's deed of acceptance of the revenue demand, signed by him. The Patta was the title deed given to the cultivator. Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar-Todar Mal?
o: Sher Shah classified land into three categories.
Akbar-Todar Mal used four land classes: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.
Akbar-Todar Mal retained the one-third share but used ten-year averages.
Sher Shah fixed the state's share at one-fourth of average produce.
x: Sher Shah's rate was one-third of average produce, not one-fourth; the other three statements are correct.

s: Under Sher Shah, to whom was the 'jaribana' fee paid?
x: Jaribana was the surveyor's fee; muhasilana was the collector's fee.

s: What was the state's share of land revenue under Sher Shah?
x: The state share was one-third of average produce; the system became the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.

s: Under Sher Shah, what was the 'muhasilana'?
o: The fee paid to the revenue collector
The fee paid to the surveyor
The title deed given to the cultivator
The deed of acceptance signed by the peasant
x: Muhasilana was the collector's fee; jaribana was the surveyor's fee.

s: On which date was the Second Battle of Panipat fought?
x: Panipat II was fought on 5 November 1556; Hemu was struck in the eye by an arrow and captured.

s: Which was the last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi?
x: The Surs were the last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi; Sher Shah's revenue, coinage and roads set the Mughal pattern.

s: Of whom was Hemu the army chief and Prime Minister?
x: Hemu (Hem Chandra Vikramaditya) was the Hindu army chief and Prime Minister of Muhammad Adil Shah.

s: How was Islam Shah (Jalal Khan), who ruled 1545-53, related to Sher Shah?
x: Islam Shah was Sher Shah's second son and ruled from 1545 to 1553.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Ushr was the land tax on Muslims. Zakat was the alms tax on Muslims, khums one-fifth of war booty and jizya the tax on non-Muslims.

s: Which one of the following pairs regarding Akbar's religious measures is correctly matched?
x: The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and jizya was abolished in 1564 according to the commonly used chronology. Some accounts place both abolitions in 1564.

s: Who drafted the Mahzar of 1579, which made Akbar supreme arbiter in religious disputes?
x: The Mahzar was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Sikandar Lodi abolished the tax on grains and several grain levies.
Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir abolished cow slaughter.
Akbar abolished the tax on grains and several grain levies.
Alauddin Khalji abolished the privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary.
x: Option C is incorrect: Sikandar Lodi, not Akbar, abolished the tax on grains. Zain-ul-Abidin banned cow slaughter, and Alauddin Khalji ended the privileges of the Khuts, Muqaddams and Chaudharis.

s: In which year did Akbar build the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri?
x: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575; 1582 is the year of Din-i-Ilahi.

s: Which one of the following represents the central meaning of Sulh-i-Kul?
o: Compulsory conversion to a single faith
x: Sulh-i-Kul means universal peace or peace with all and served as a guiding principle of Akbar's policy.

s: With the death of which emperor did Din-i-Ilahi, joined by only a handful of people, lapse?
x: Din-i-Ilahi lapsed with Akbar and did not continue as a major institution.

s: In Islamic taxation, what did 'Khums' mean?
x: Khums was one-fifth of war booty; Ushr was land tax, Zakat alms tax and Haqq-e-Sharb irrigation tax.

s: In which year did Akbar abolish the pilgrimage tax?
x: The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and jizya in 1564.

s: Which ruler abolished the grain tax?
x: The grain tax was ended by Sikandar Lodi, not Akbar.

s: In which year was Akbar's Ibadat Khana opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians?
x: Built in 1575 for Muslim divines, the Ibadat Khana was opened to all faiths in 1578.

s: Akbar issued coins with figures of Rama and Sita bearing which Devanagari legend?
x: Akbar's Rama-Sita coins carry the Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'.

s: Which Mughal emperor ended the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad at the request of Kavindracharya?
x: Shah Jahan ended the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad after Kavindracharya and the Banaras pandits asked.

s: In medieval Islamic taxation, what was 'Haqq-e-Sharb'?
x: Haqq-e-Sharb was the irrigation tax; zakat was alms tax and ushr land tax on Muslims.

s: Which of the following was NOT a feature associated with Din-i-Ilahi?
o: Reverence for the sun and fire
x: Din-i-Ilahi included belief in one God, reverence for the sun and fire, and avoidance of meat-eating. It was never forcibly imposed on anyone.

s: Why did Din-i-Ilahi not become a mass religion?
o: Was confined to the Rajput nobility
Was abolished by Akbar soon after its launch
Was never forced on anyone and drew only a small circle
Was banned by the ulema in 1579
x: Its voluntary nature and small membership explain why Din-i-Ilahi never became a mass religion.

s: By what title was Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi known?
x: Sirhindi was Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani and propounded Wahdat-ul-Shuhud.

s: Who among the following criticised Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul from an orthodox Islamic standpoint?
x: Badauni and the Naqshbandi scholar Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar's religious innovations, including Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul.

s: Din-i-Ilahi had about how many members?
x: Din-i-Ilahi was a small voluntary circle of about 18 members.

s: Who is regarded as the chief exponent ('prophet') of Din-i-Ilahi?
x: Abul Fazl was its chief exponent; Badauni and Ahmad Sirhindi were its orthodox critics.

s: To which Sufi order did Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, known as Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, belong?
x: Ahmad Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi, the most orthodox order, and criticised Akbar's religious ideas.

s: Who among the following called Din-i-Ilahi a religion in his Dabistan-i-Mazahib?
x: Mohsin Fani, a contemporary of Jahangir, called it a religion in the Dabistan-i-Mazahib.

s: Who led the first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court (1580)?
x: The first Jesuit mission from Goa in 1580 was led by Rudolf Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate; Jerome Xavier led the third mission in 1595.

s: Under whose leadership was the third Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1595 conducted?
x: The third Jesuit mission, sent in 1595, was under Jerome Xavier.

s: With the growth of which city is Akbar's grant of land to Guru Ram Das associated?
x: Land granted to Guru Ram Das became associated with the growth of Amritsar.

s: On which Jain scholar did Akbar confer the title 'Yuga Pradhan'?
x: Jinachandra Suri was called Yuga Pradhan; Hiravijaya Suri received the title Jagat Guru.

s: Which Parsi priest received a land grant from Akbar?
x: Dastur Meherji Rana, a Parsi, received a land grant; Xavier and Acquaviva were Jesuits.

s: In which year did the second Jesuit mission from Goa reach Akbar's court?
x: The Jesuit missions came in 1580, 1591 and 1595; 1591 was the second.

s: Who was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi?
x: Birbal was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi. The circle of members was small, numbering about 18 according to the cited account.

s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose jizya?
x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679 and banned festivals such as Navroz.

s: Which of the following about Akbar's religious measures is NOT correct?
o: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575.
The Mahzar preceded the construction of the Ibadat Khana.
x: The Mahzar (1579) came after the Ibadat Khana (1575); the order is jizya abolished 1564, Ibadat Khana 1575, Mahzar 1579, Din-i-Ilahi 1582.

s: The first Jesuit Mission is associated with which year?
x: The first Jesuit mission reached Akbar in 1580; 1800 is the Serampore Mission and 1942 the Cripps Mission.

s: In which year was Akbar crowned at Kalanaur?
x: Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur in 1556 after Humayun died in January that year.

s: Where was Bairam Khan, Akbar's regent (1556-60), going when he was killed in 1561?
x: Dismissed in 1560, Bairam Khan was killed on the way to Mecca in 1561.

s: Whose dominance does the expression 'petticoat government' in Akbar's early reign refer to?
o: Ruqaiya Sultan Begum and Man Singh I
Hamida Banu Begum and Salima Sultan Begum
Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan
x: The term refers to the period from 1560 to 1564 when Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan exercised considerable influence.

s: Against whom did Akbar's forces fight the Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556), which ended Afghan power?
x: At Panipat II (1556) Hemu was hit in the eye by an arrow and captured, ending Afghan power. Daud Khan Karrani opposed Akbar in Bengal (1576), Baz Bahadur in Malwa (1561), and Ibrahim Lodi lost the First Battle of Panipat (1526) to Babur.

s: On which date was Akbar enthroned?
x: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556, after Humayun's death. The 1658 and 1659 dates are Aurangzeb's two coronations.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Iltutmish declared himself Sultan at Delhi.
Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place at Kalanaur.
Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur, Gurdaspur, Punjab.
x: Option C is incorrect: Aurangzeb's first coronation was at Delhi, not Kalanaur; Kalanaur is where Akbar was enthroned. Iltutmish at Delhi, Shivaji at Raigarh and Akbar at Kalanaur are right.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Shivaji – Worshipped at Buddha's birthplace, Lumbini
Akbar – Under 14 years of age at coronation
Ashoka – Succession backed by Turkish nobles
x: Akbar was only 13 when crowned. Turkish nobles backed Iltutmish, Shivaji was crowned at Raigarh and Ashoka worshipped at Lumbini.

s: For murdering whom did Akbar personally kill Adham Khan in 1562?
x: Adham Khan, son of Maham Anaga, was killed by Akbar in 1562 for murdering Atagh Khan.

s: Where was Akbar born in 1542?
x: Akbar was born on 15 October 1542 at Amarkot; Kalanaur is where he was crowned in 1556.

s: On which date did Aurangzeb's first coronation take place at Delhi?
x: Aurangzeb was first crowned at Delhi on 21 July 1658, before Deorai; his second coronation was on 5 June 1659 after Khajwa and Deorai.

s: Who opposed Akbar in Gondwana?
x: Rani Durgavati opposed Akbar in Gondwana; Baz Bahadur in Malwa, Rana Udai Singh at Chittor, Surjan Rai at Ranthambore.

s: With which conquest was Akbar's last campaign associated?
o: Gujarat, where Buland Darwaza was built
Khandesh, including the capture of Asirgarh fort
x: Akbar's last campaign was the conquest of Khandesh in 1601, during which the Asirgarh fort was taken from Miran Bahadur.

s: Akbar's empire stretched from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to which river?
x: Akbar's empire extended from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the Godavari.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Akbar conquered Gujarat in 1572–73, opposing Muzaffar Shah III. Daud Khan Karrani was associated with Bengal, Mirza Hakim with Kabul, and Chand Bibi with Ahmednagar.

s: From whom did Akbar annex Kashmir in 1586?
x: Kashmir was taken in 1586 from Yusuf Shah Chak; Miran Bahadur was of Khandesh and Baz Bahadur of Malwa.

s: Who resisted Akbar's capture of Ahmednagar in 1600?
x: Chand Bibi defended Ahmednagar (1600); Rani Durgavati resisted in Gondwana (1564).

s: Which of the following pairs (Region – opponent of Akbar) is correctly matched?
x: Ranthambore (1569) was held by Surjan Rai Hada; Malwa was Baz Bahadur's, Bengal Daud Khan's, Kabul Mirza Hakim's and Khandesh Miran Bahadur's.

s: From whom did Akbar conquer Malwa in 1561?
x: Malwa was taken in 1561 from the Afghan ruler Baz Bahadur.

s: Who was the ruler of Mewar when Akbar captured Chittor in 1568?
x: Chittor fell in 1568 during the rule of Rana Udai Singh.

s: In which year did Akbar capture Chittor?
x: Akbar took Chittor in 1568 and Ranthambore in 1569.

s: Who was the Afghan ruler of Bengal whom Akbar's forces defeated in 1576?
x: Bengal (with Bihar) was conquered in 1576 from Daud Khan Karrani, son of Sulaiman.

s: Against whom did Akbar march to Kabul in 1581?
x: In 1581 Akbar marched on Kabul against his half-brother Mirza Hakim.

s: Which state did Tansen's early patron, Raja Ramchandra Singh, rule?
x: Tansen was first patronised by Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa before joining Akbar's court as a Navaratna.

s: Under what name was the Mahabharata translated in Akbar's time?
x: The Mahabharata was rendered as the Razmnama; the Atharvaveda was also translated.

s: Who wrote Akbarnama and was associated with Akbar as a scholar and court intellectual?
x: Abul Fazl, Akbar's court historian, wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari and rendered the Panchatantra as Ayar-i-Danish. Faizi was his brother and poet laureate.

s: Who translated the Baburnama into Persian?
x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, son of Bairam Khan, translated the Baburnama into Persian.

s: What was Akbar's translation bureau at Fatehpur Sikri called?
x: The Maktab Khana ('House of Translation') was Akbar's translation bureau; the Ibadat Khana was the hall of religious debate.

s: Around which year was Akbar's Maktab Khana set up?
x: The Maktab Khana was set up at Fatehpur Sikri around 1574.

s: Who translated the Yogavasistha into Persian under Akbar?
x: Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Yogavasistha; Abdur Rahim translated the Baburnama.

s: Which of the following about Fatehpur Sikri is NOT correct?
o: The Buland Darwaza there commemorates the conquest of Bengal.
The Ibadat Khana was built there in 1575.
The first Jesuit mission reached it in 1580.
x: The Buland Darwaza commemorates the Gujarat conquest (1572-73), not Bengal.

s: While fighting whom was Raja Birbal killed in 1586?
x: Birbal was killed in 1586 fighting the Yusufzai.

s: By whom was Abul Fazl murdered in 1602?
o: Man Singh I at Akbar's instance
Adham Khan at Bairam Khan's instance
Bir Singh Bundela at Salim's instance
x: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by Bir Singh Bundela at the instance of Prince Salim.

s: Which one of Akbar's court figures, originally named Ramtanu Pandey, is associated with the ragas Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi?
x: Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey) was the court musician credited with Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi. Faizi was the poet laureate, Birbal (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser, and Abdur Rahim a poet known for Hindi dohas.

s: Which conquest of Akbar does the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri commemorate?
x: The Buland Darwaza marks the Gujarat conquest of 1572-73.

s: Who translated the Lilavati into Persian in Akbar's time?
x: Faizi, Akbar's poet laureate and Abul Fazl's brother, made the Persian Lilavati.

s: Under what name did Abul Fazl render the Panchatantra into Persian?
x: Abul Fazl's Persian Panchatantra is the Ayar-i-Danish.

s: Who was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi?
x: Sheikh Mubarak, who drafted the Mahzar, was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi.

s: Which title did Akbar confer on Tansen?
x: Akbar gave Tansen the title 'Miyan' (hence Miyan ki Malhar); the name Tansen came from an earlier Hindu patron.

s: Rao Chandrasena, who never surrendered to Akbar, was the ruler of which state?
x: Rao Chandrasena of Marwar resisted from Bhadrajun, Siwana and Sojat until his death in 1581.

s: The Battle of Haldighati formed part of Akbar's campaign against which state?
x: The Battle of Haldighati was part of Akbar's Mewar campaign. It was fought between the Mughal forces led by Man Singh and Maharana Pratap.

s: Who led the Mughal side in the Battle of Haldighati (1576)?
x: Man Singh led Akbar's forces against Rana Pratap at Haldighati in 1576.

s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Akbar's Rajput policy?
o: Appointment of Rajputs to high posts
Immediate loss of autonomy for every Rajput state after submission
x: Submission could be followed by restoration of autonomy and honour, so blanket loss of autonomy was not part of the policy.

s: With whose daughter did Akbar enter into a matrimonial alliance in 1562?
x: In 1562, Akbar married the daughter of Raja Bharmal of Amber, a Kachhwaha ruler.

s: Under which Mughal emperor did Mewar finally submit through Rana Amar Singh's treaty of 1615?
x: Mewar held out against Akbar and submitted only under Jahangir in 1615; Karan Singh became a mansabdar.

s: In which language was Babur's memoir, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi, written?
x: Babur wrote in Turki; Jahangir's Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri was in Persian.

s: Which Mughal emperor was unlettered but introduced educational reforms covering arithmetic, logic, astronomy and agriculture?
x: Akbar could not read or write, yet he was a great patron of learning and widened the curriculum.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Humayun was learned in Persian, Arabic and Turkish.
2. Jahangir wrote his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, in Persian.
3. Akbar wrote an autobiography in Turki.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Humayun was learned and Jahangir wrote in Persian; Akbar was unlettered and wrote no autobiography.

s: In which language did Jahangir write his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
x: Jahangir wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri in Persian, unlike Babur, who wrote in Turki.

s: Which statement regarding Raja Todar Mal is correct?
o: He served Aurangzeb and had earlier served Murshid Quli Khan.
He served only the Qutb Shahis and introduced the Pargana system.
He was a provincial Qazi who designed the Mansabdari system.
He served Akbar and had earlier served Sher Shah.
x: Todar Mal was Akbar's revenue minister and had earlier served Sher Shah. His system was modelled on Sher Shah's survey-based arrangements.

s: Who designed the Zabti or Dahsala system?
x: Raja Todar Mal designed the Zabti, also called Bandobast or Dahsala, revenue system.

s: In Mughal revenue practice, what did 'Kankut' mean?
o: A fixed cash rate per bigha
x: Kankut estimated the standing crop; Batai was crop-sharing and Nasaq was based on past payments.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Mughal revenue is correctly matched?
o: Dahsala (Zabti) – Average produce and prices over ten years
x: The Dahsala used ten-year average produce and prices. The state took one-third, the cultivator kept two-thirds, and Haqq-e-Sharb was an irrigation tax.

s:
Consider the following statements about the mansabdari system:
1. It was introduced by Akbar.
2. The Dagh system of horse branding dates from 1573-74.
3. Du-aspa sih-aspa was first granted to Mahabat Khan by Akbar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; du-aspa sih-aspa was introduced by Jahangir, not Akbar.

s: Under Akbar's Karori experiment (1574), how much revenue was each circle meant to yield?
x: Each circle was to yield one crore dams, hence the name 'karori'.

s: What did the mansabdari and zabti-dahsala systems together give the Mughal state?
o: A salaried, transferable nobility and predictable cash revenue
A hereditary nobility and tribute from autonomous chiefs
Religious endowments in place of military service
Revenue in kind collected directly from every village
x: Mansabdari and zabti-dahsala together provided a salaried, transferable nobility and a predictable stream of cash revenue.

s: In which year was Akbar's Karori experiment introduced?
x: The Karori experiment was in 1574; the Dahsala followed in 1580.

s: Under the Karori experiment, what were the officers in charge of the revenue circles called?
x: Each circle yielding one crore dams was under an officer called a karori.

s: Upon whose earlier survey-based system did Todar Mal's revenue arrangements build?
x: Todar Mal had earlier served Sher Shah and built upon Sher Shah's survey-based system.

s: Of what was the improved jarib made, which avoided shrinking or stretching in land measurement?
o: Bamboo pieces joined with iron rings
x: The jarib was made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings, which avoided the shrinkage or stretching of hemp rope.

s: Todar Mal held which office in the Mughal Empire?
x: Todar Mal served as the Diwan, or finance minister, of the empire and was also counted among the Navratnas.

s: Which of the following about the state share under Todar Mal's revenue arrangement is NOT correct?
o: It was one-third of the average produce.
It was normally paid in cash called dam.
Payment in kind was allowed in some areas.
It was paid in cash called jital.
x: The state share was paid in cash called dam, not jital, though payment in kind was allowed in some areas.

s: About how long was the Gaz-i-Ilahi, Akbar's unit of length?
x: The Gaz-i-Ilahi was about 82 cm.

s: Who was the first to be given the proper status of Diwan by Akbar, with Todar Mal as his assistant?
x: Akbar first gave the proper status of Diwan to Muzaffar Khan Turbati; Todar Mal and Khwaja Shah Mansur came later.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zabti — Crop-sharing between the state and peasant
Batai — Rough assessment based on past revenue records
Kankut — Yield estimated on the standing crop
Nasaq — Land measured and cash rates fixed per crop
x: Kankut involved estimating the yield on the standing crop. Zabti involved measurement and cash rates, Batai involved crop-sharing, and Nasaq relied on past revenue records.

s: In which region was the Nasaq method of revenue assessment mainly used under the Mughals?
x: Nasaq was used mainly in Bengal; Batai in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir, Zabti in the core provinces, plough-based assessment in parts of the Deccan.

s: In which year was Akbar's Dahsala system introduced?
x: Dahsala, based on ten-year average produce and prices commuted into cash, came in 1580; 1574 was the Karori experiment.

s: The Dahsala was based on the average produce and prices of which years?
x: The Dahsala (1580) used the average of the last ten years, 1571-1580.

s: Where was Batai (Ghalla-bakhshi) mainly used under the Mughals?
x: Crop-sharing (batai) was used in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir; Nasaq was mainly in Bengal and Zabti in the core provinces.

s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, what were the 'dasturs'?
o: Cash revenue rates per crop per bigha
Revenue circles yielding one crore dams
x: Under zabti, land was measured and dasturs fixed cash rates per crop per bigha.

s: In parts of the Deccan, on what basis was land revenue fixed under the plough method?
o: An estimate of the standing crop
x: In parts of the Deccan revenue was assessed by the number of ploughs.

s: What was Mughal crown land, whose revenue went straight to the imperial treasury, called?
x: Crown land was khalisa; suyurghal and madad-i-maash were charitable revenue-free grants.

s: What did a jagir represent under the Mughal system?
o: A direct cash payment from the khalisa treasury
The right to collect revenue in lieu of salary, without ownership
A permanent revenue-free grant to scholars
x: A jagir was an assignment of the right to collect revenue in lieu of salary; it did not confer ownership of the land.

s: What were Mughal revenue-free grants to scholars, holy men and the needy called?
x: Madad-i-maash (also suyurghal) was a charitable revenue-free grant; Khalisa was crown land.

s: What was the principal source of income of the Mughal state?
x: Maal, the land revenue, was the main income of the Mughal state.

s: What did the term 'Suyurghal' mean in the Mughal period?
x: Suyurghal, like madad-i-maash, was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy.

s: Under the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the state generally took what share of the produce?
x: Golconda generally took one-third of the produce, not one-half.

s: Which Mughal official kept the land and revenue records of a pargana?
x: The qanungo kept pargana land and revenue records; the potdar was a treasurer.

s: What was the Potdar in Mughal revenue administration?
x: The potdar was the treasurer; the patwari was the village accountant and the amalguzar the sarkar revenue collector.

s: In Mughal revenue administration, what was the duty of the Bitikchi?
o: Collecting the revenue of the sarkar
Keeping records on land and produce
Maintaining law and order in towns
x: The bitikchi kept records on land and produce; the amalguzar collected revenue and the potdar was treasurer.

s: Who was the revenue collector of a Mughal sarkar, also charged with extending cultivation?
x: The amalguzar collected sarkar revenue and tried to extend cultivation.

s: From about which period do the dual ranks of Zat and Sawar in Akbar's mansabdari date?
x: Zat and Sawar dual ranks came about 1595-96; 1573-74 was the Dagh system.

s: Who introduced the du-aspa sih-aspa system?
x: Du-aspa sih-aspa was Jahangir's measure, first for Mahabat Khan; Zat-Sawar was Akbar's.

s: Which of the following pairs (Land assignment – Rulers) is NOT correctly matched?
x: Mokasa was the Maratha assignment; the Mughals used jagirs.

s: Which feature distinguished Mughal mansabdars from the British ICS?
o: They were paid only fixed treasury salaries
x: Mansabdars held combined civil-military, non-hereditary ranks paid by jagir; the ICS was purely civil and salaried.

s: In which tradition did the Mughal mansabdari system have its origin?
x: Mansabdari was of Central Asian / Mongol military origin.

s: Under Akbar, to whom alone were mansabs above those of the nobles (5,000, later 7,000) given?
x: Noble ranks ran from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks were only for royal princes.

s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's mansabdari system:
1. Zat denoted personal rank and pay.
2. Sawar denoted the number of horsemen to be maintained.
3. Mansabs were hereditary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Zat was personal rank and Sawar the horsemen to be kept; mansabs were non-hereditary.

s: In which class was a mansabdar whose sawar rank equalled his zat rank placed?
x: By the sawar-zat ratio, sawar equal to zat made a mansabdar first class.

s: What was the range of mansab ranks for nobles under Akbar?
x: Nobles held mansabs from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks went only to princes.

s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, how was land that had been left fallow for three to four years classified?
x: Chachar was land fallow for 3-4 years. Polaj was cultivated every year, Parauti was fallow for 1-2 years, and Banjar was uncultivated for 5 years or more.

s: Under Akbar's land classification, what was land left fallow for one or two years called?
x: Parauti lay fallow one or two years; Polaj was cultivated every year, Chachar fallow three or four years, Banjar five or more.

s: Under Akbar's land classification, what was land left uncultivated for five years or more called?
x: Banjar was fallow 5+ years; Parauti 1-2 and Chachar 3-4 years.

s: In Akbar's classification, what kind of land was Polaj?
x: Polaj land was cultivated every year.

s: What condition is described as the jagirdari crisis under Aurangzeb?
o: Too many jagirdars competing for too few jagirs, placing pressure on the peasantry
The complete abolition of jagirs by Akbar
The transfer of all jagirs to Rajput rulers
Too few mansabdars controlling an excessive number of jagirs
x: The jagirdari crisis arose because too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs, which increased pressure on the peasantry.

s: Which type of Mughal jagir was hereditary and not transferable?
x: Watan jagir, the zamindar's homeland, was hereditary and not transferable.

s: After how many years were Tankha jagirs, given in lieu of salary, normally transferred?
x: Tankha jagirs were transferable every 3-4 years, which prevented local power bases.

s: Which of the following pairs (Jagir type – feature) is correctly matched?
o: Mashrut – conditional, tied to specified duties
x: Mashrut was conditional; Watan was non-transferable, In'am carried no service obligation and Tankha was in lieu of salary.

s: Which Mughal central minister handled military matters such as dagh, chehra and promotions?
x: The Mir Bakhshi was the military head in charge of dagh, chehra and promotions.

s: What was the Mughal Sadr-us-sudur in charge of?
x: The Sadr-us-sudur dealt with religious affairs, charitable grants and the Shariat.

s: Which of the following about Mughal central ministers is NOT correct?
o: The Mir Saman was in charge of religious affairs.
The Wakil was the highest in rank.
The Wazir handled revenue, treasury and accounts.
x: The Mir Saman looked after the royal household and karkhanas; religious affairs were with the Sadr-us-sudur.

s: Which Mughal central minister looked after the royal household and the karkhanas?
x: The Mir Saman was in charge of the royal household and karkhanas.

s: Who was the head of a Mughal suba, served by a Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi?
x: The Subedar headed the suba; the Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi were the other suba officials.

s: Which of the following pairs (Unit – Officials) is correctly matched?
x: The pargana had the shiqdar, amil and qanungo. The sarkar had the faujdar and amalguzar, the town the kotwal, and the village the muqaddam, patwari and chowkidar.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Faujdar — military and law-and-order duties at the sarkar level
Subahdar — governor responsible for law and order
Provincial Diwan — revenue administration and an independent check on the governor
Kotwal — maintenance of pargana land and revenue records
x: The Kotwal was responsible for law and order in the city. Maintenance of land and revenue records at the pargana level was the duty of the Qanungo.

s: In 1580, Akbar's empire was divided into how many subas?
x: There were 12 subas in 1580.

s: Whose duty was law and order in a Mughal town?
x: The kotwal kept law and order in the city; the faujdar did so at sarkar level.
